A vertical milling operation is performed on a lathed part using a vertical milling machine for 13 minutes, employing an end mill tool at a milling speed of 800 rpm and a depth of cut of 2.5 mm, resulting in a milled part that is transferred to a conveyor belt.

A Wire EDM (Electrical Discharge Machine) performs wire EDM cutting on a shaped part loaded from a MobileRobot, using brass-coated zinc wire at electrical parameters of 15 A and 50 V and a cutting speed of 4 mm/min, producing a precision finished part that is transferred to a ConveyorBelt, with the operation lasting for 54 minutes.

Using a Stewart Platform Mills machine, the milled part is subjected to precision milling for 47 minutes with a milling precision of ±0.01 mm, a 6-axis simultaneous tool configuration, and an active damping system for vibration control, after which the resulting ground part is placed on a conveyor belt.

A metal bar is loaded onto a mobile robot and machined on a horizontal lathe using horizontal turning at a rotation speed of 700 rpm and a feed rate of 0.2 mm/rev with a ceramic insert tool for 81 minutes, resulting in a lathed part that is transferred to a conveyor belt.

The milled part is machined using a horizontal milling operation on a horizontal milling machine at a milling speed of 750 rpm with a climb milling tool path to achieve a surface finish of Ra 1.6 µm, taking 96 minutes, after which the finished machined component is placed on a conveyor belt.

On the Gear Shaper, gear shaping is performed on the broached component to produce a shaped gear, forming a spur gear with 24 teeth at a shaping speed of 120 strokes/min, and the operation runs for 69 minutes, after which the shaped gear is placed on the ConveyorBelt.

On the Honing Machine, a honing operation is performed on the Honed cylinder to achieve precision finishing, using a 150 mesh honing grit to achieve a bore size of 50 mm, lasting for 74 minutes, after which the resulting Precision finished part is transferred to the ConveyorBelt.

The punch press performs a punching operation on a sheet metal component, using a 10 mm punch size and automatic die alignment at a stroke speed of 80 strokes per minute, processing the material for 91 minutes to produce a finished sheet metal product that is then transferred to a conveyor belt.

The milled part is shaped on a Shaper using a high-speed steel tool with a stroke length of 300 mm and a shaping speed of 40 strokes per minute, lasting for 67 minutes, after which the resulting shaped part is placed on a ConveyorBelt.

A planed part is loaded from a mobile robot onto a grinding machine where it undergoes surface grinding using an aluminum oxide grinding wheel rotating at 1800 m/min with a feed rate of 0.05 mm/pass, transforming it into a ground part that is then transferred to a conveyor belt, all taking 89 minutes.

On the Hobbing Machine, a gear hobbing operation is performed on a broached component to create an involute gear profile, running at a hobbing speed of 150 rpm with a feed rate of 0.3 mm/rev for 81 minutes, resulting in a hobbied gear that is transferred to a conveyor belt.

The Stewart Platform Mills perform precision grinding on the milled part loaded from the MobileRobot, using a diamond-coated grinding tool with high-precision mode activated for fine surface tolerance and an active damping system engaged to minimize harmonic oscillations, transforming it into a ground part that is then placed on the ConveyorBelt for 64 minutes.

The milled part is subjected to surface planing on a planer for 88 minutes, achieving flat surface generation with a planing depth of 2.5 mm per pass, a feed rate of 150 mm/min for consistent material removal, and a target surface finish of Ra 3.2 µm using a fine cutting tool, resulting in a planed part transferred to a mobile robot.

On a CNC Turning Center, a CNC turning operation is performed for 30 minutes to complete the final contouring of a lathed part using CNC program #TC-09, with tool offsets automatically calibrated via a touch-probe system and a spindle speed of 1100 rpm for the finish pass on alloy steel, resulting in a finished machined component that is transferred to a mobile robot.

The Shear (Sheet Metal) machine performs a shearing operation on sheet metal, using high-carbon steel blades with a hardened edge, a shear angle of 1.5 degrees to reduce deformation and burr formation, and a cutting speed of 20 strokes per minute for clean edge quality, transforming the input sheet metal into sheared sheet metal over a duration of 77 minutes, with the output transferred to a ConveyorBelt.

The shaper performs a shaping operation on the milled part, using a high-speed steel single-point cutting tool with a stroke length of 150 mm to match the workpiece profile and a shaping speed of 30 double strokes per minute for controlled cut, transforming the milled part into a shaped part over a duration of 97 minutes, after which the shaped part is transferred to the mobile robot.
